math-k2.verdict:
Mostly fixed. Both blockers are fixed and hold up under independent checks. Three findings are only partly fixed, and the fix added a few small hint and read-aloud problems. No wrong answer keys were found.

How I checked: worktree at fbd7dfe, clean afterwards. I dumped 58,400 items (all 25 skills × all levels × 400 seeds × en/es) and checked them with my own Python parsers.

Verified fixed:
- **Blocker 1 (fraction bars).** I read every bar prompt with my own en/es share tables and tried every state the pad can reach (parts 1–4, every shading). In all 4,000 bar items × 2 languages, exactly one state is accepted, and it is the cut and shading the words ask for. "1/1" is rejected and tagged did-not-cut. The same amount on another cut (2/4 for one half, 2/2 or 4/4 for all thirds) is rejected and tagged made-X-not-Y. Every tag matches what was built.
- **Blocker 2 (left/right on phones).** m.compare.groups and m.data.picture are no longer markable, so they draw as the plain DotsVisual, an SVG that scales down and never wraps. I ran the real layoutCounters at 286, 341, 396 and 654 px. No markable item that uses left/right/izquierda/derecha wraps. The only wrapping items that use position words say "first group" or "first frame", which still read correctly when stacked.
- **Coins.** Re-valuing every option with nickel and dime swapped gave 0 mismatches over 420 "Which coins" items. The swap tag sits on exactly the set a swapper would pick and on nothing else. The count items' swap values are right, and no tag is emitted when the swap changes nothing.
- **Other majors.** take-add: 96/96 stories have c ≤ b. Ruler L3 say and prompt use full unit words, with "in."/"pulg."/"cm" only after the blank. m.measure.units L2 pairs are realistic, and the alt texts now match what is drawn.
- **Minors.** All fixed: "1 is/1 está" singular; no swapped-pair duplicates in decompose L2 (always 4 choices); place.1000 L3 always has 3 or more choices; no 12:00 clock answers; every clock item lists a wrong value; the why tags (crossed-out, tens-digit on dots, empty boxes on a full frame, shown numbers as filler); compare and tensFirst hints; data.chart recoded to 2.OA.A.1; every listed Spanish line. A scan for key numbers in hints found no remaining leak in m.story.100.

Outside this audit's scope: the shared tensFirst helper has the Spanish slip "10 son 1 decena" (should be "10 es 1 decena"). It appears in m.mental.100, m.story.100 and m.measure.ruler and was there before the fix.

Test run: the full related suites have 3,446 of 3,447 passing. The one failure is the k2-more "every item" test, which hit its fixed 60 s timeout twice when the whole file ran on this heavily loaded machine (load average 45–200). Run alone it passes in about 21 s. That looks like load-dependent flakiness, not a content problem.

Nothing was committed. The scratch harness and dump are deleted, and the worktree is clean at fbd7dfe.

unfixed.finding: major — measuring pictures (m.measure.units L1, m.measure.ruler L1-2)
unfixed.problem: Only the interim fix landed for the ruler. The object is still not drawn on the ruler: the number-line shows only the end dot. At L2 the start point ("starts at 1") still exists only in the text, so the item is plain subtraction on a number line, not measuring. m.measure.units L1 now shows a bar of touching blocks, which fixes the dots-vs-cubes complaint. But the bar is always drawn full width (4 blocks look as long as 11), it is not drawn next to the object, and the alt still says "as long as the ribbon".
unfixed.fix: Draw the measured object as a segment on the ruler from s to the end, and draw the start for L2 (a second marker, or a shaded span on the number-line visual). For the units bar, scale its width with n, or drop "as long as the X" from the alt.

unfixed.finding: major — tiny item pools (m.shares.halves L1-2, m.shares.thirds L1-2)
unfixed.problem: These levels reach the 12-distinct floor only by changing the whole's noun and emoji (8 WHOLES). With the noun removed, the distinct tasks per level are still 5 (halves L1), 6 (halves L2), 9 (thirds L1) and 6 (thirds L2). No new shape (rectangle or circle) and no new question type ('which bar shows thirds', 'is this cut into equal shares?') was added, so a child can still learn the handful of tasks by heart. The new variety test also counts the sorted choice labels, so a level with few distinct questions passes on distractor variety alone; m.decompose.10 L2 has only 7 distinct prompts (not in the original list).
unfixed.fix: Add at least one new question type or shape per shares level (an equal vs not-equal shares choice, 'which picture shows fourths', a rectangle or circle visual), and count variety on prompt + visual + picture only, without choices.

unfixed.finding: minor — standard codes
unfixed.problem: Only m.data.chart was recoded (to 2.OA.A.1). m.measure.ruler is still coded 2.MD.A.1 although L3 tests 2.MD.A.2 and 2.MD.A.4. m.place.1000 is still coded 2.NBT.A.1 although L2-L3 (expanded form, number names) are 2.NBT.A.3. m.data.picture (1.MD.C.4) is still unlabelled dot groups.
unfixed.fix: Recode or split m.measure.ruler L3 and m.place.1000 L2-3, or add the extra standards. Label the data.picture groups with category icons or names.

newProblems: Minor: some hints added or exposed by the fix show the answer. The fix's own test only scans equations, so all of these pass it: (a) m.decompose.10 L1's new hint 3, "Say a. Then count on: a+1, …", shows the answer whenever b = a+1, e.g. '7 = 3 + ▢' → 'Say 3. Then count on: 4, …' (54/400 items, 13.5%). (b) m.count.100 now starts at 0, so '0, ▢, 20, 30' gets the fixed hint 'Count by tens out loud, starting at 10.', and 10 is the answer (18/400 at L1, 4/400 at L3). (c) The new dots variant of m.write.20 L1 has the hint 'Start at the left: 1, 2…', which is the answer when n = 2 and counts past the only dot when n = 1 (30 of 133 dot items). (d) m.measure.units L1 can now be 3 blocks long, so 'Point to each block as you count: 1, 2, 3…' ends on the answer (35/400). Fix: don't print a count-on number in decompose ('Say a, then keep counting until you say n'), make the 'starting at …' hint depend on the first number shown, and drop the literal '1, 2…' / '1, 2, 3…' when n ≤ 3.

Minor: Spanish coin items now use the US coin names ('Tienes 1 nickel y 7 pennies', 'Un dime vale 10¢'). That fixes the value-given problem, but these lines go to an es-US text-to-speech voice, which will say the English words with Spanish sounds. 'dime' is also a Spanish word ('tell me'), so 'Tienes 1 dime' can be heard as nonsense by K–2 children who rely on read-aloud. Fix: in Spanish `say` only, use a spoken spelling or a name-plus-gloss that does not give the value, or check the es-US voice output.

Minor tradeoff: to keep groups in one row, m.compare.groups (K) and m.data.picture (grade 1) lost tap-to-mark counting. m.measure.units L1 lost it too when its picture became a bar. K–1 children now count and match up to 10 + 10 or 3 × 5 static dots that render about 12–18 px wide at 320 px, while the hints still say 'Match dots one to one' and 'Point to each dot'. The audit's other option (a markable layout that shrinks cells instead of wrapping) would keep the aid.

eng-reading-35.verdict:
Mostly fixed. All five major findings were dealt with, the minor fixes I checked are correct, and the passage split in 8391b34 changed no content: PASSAGES and PAIRS serialize identically to the single file at d34f845.

What I re-checked independently:
- Keys: 9 skills × 2 levels × 400 seeds × en/es, 14,400 items. I matched each item back to its passage and question by text alone, and for narrator items I worked out first or third person from my own pronoun scan of the narration outside quotes. Result: 0 key mismatches. The checker accepts only the key. Labels are distinct, every wrong choice has a valid tag, and the key index is the same in both languages. No hint contains the key, there are no unbalanced or nested quotes, no ASCII quotes in hints or steps, and no English leaks into the Spanish.
- Point of view: the narrator question is now 31% of the L1 pool and 28% of L2 (4 of 14 in each), and it has 3 choices.
- Repeats inside a set: practice sets showed 0 repeats in 3,000 sets for every skill. e.text.features hit the 100-draw fallback once in 6,000 sets. Checks, review sets and mixed sets showed 0 repeats.
- Display: the passage is classified into paragraphs, headings and boxes the same way in both languages for all 19 articles. Runner keeps only the question in the h1.
- Read as a teacher and a native Spanish speaker: the content diff, every new point-of-view question, every new hint 2 for text features, and all changed passages and pairs. These are now right: launch-day message and key; science-fair two rooms; city-rain ending; egg-stand "handed me"; camels "large animals… without water"; drums question; hummingbird distractor; retags for kite, coral, coral pair and moon pair Q3; quote fixes for two-lanterns and the moon pair; tamales and new-school asked neutrally; the pier grandson; and the Spanish fixes for botas, gol, colibrí, segundo puesto, anciana Rut, inquieto, punto caliente, equilibraba, descarapelada and tenía futuro.
- URLs: no URL changed in the diff, so there was nothing to re-fetch.
- Tests: the full web suite passed, 4,091 tests. On the first full run one test in k2-more.test.ts failed (vitest's report pointed at its MATH_K_2_MORE loop); the file passes when run alone and passed on a full re-run. This strand did not touch it.

Setup note: `git reset --hard` was blocked by the permission system. The worktree was clean and d8d8166 is an ancestor of f373586, so I used `git merge --ff-only` to move it to f373586 instead. That moved the worktree branch's pointer forward, which may make the harness treat the worktree as changed. Nothing was committed, and I deleted my scratch files; the tree is clean.

unfixed.finding: major: pools of 13–19 entries per level, so sets and checks repeat items (reading-35.ts pools + learning/engine.ts)
unfixed.problem: Only half was fixed. Repeats inside one set are gone, but the second half of the audit's fix ("grow each level to at least 25 entries before treating checks as evidence") was not done: pools are still 13–19 per level (point of view grew to 14). Example with e.text.features L2 (13 entries): a 10-item practice set shows 10 of the 13, so the 5-item check that follows has on average 3.85 items (77%) the learner just practiced with feedback and worked steps. All 5 were just practiced 19.6% of the time (C(10,5)/C(13,5)). Retakes draw from the same 13, so remembered answers still count toward checks.
unfixed.fix: Grow each level to at least 25 entries. Until then, have buildCheckSlots skip seeds the learner saw in recent sets of the same skill, or keep reading checks out of evidence while the bank is draft.

unfixed.finding: minor: tutor check_answer accepts only an exact label match (apps/web/src/lib/ai/tools.ts:82)
unfixed.problem: Unchanged by this fix. `findIndex(c => c.label.trim().toLowerCase() === answer...)` still needs the whole sentence-long reading label. A learner who says "the second one" or "a narrator outside the story" is checked as index -1 and told they are wrong.
unfixed.fix: Also accept a choice number or letter and the key's content words, or pass the choice index from the UI. Add a test that uses a reading item.

unfixed.finding: minor: hint 1 hands over the answer as an either/or
unfixed.problem: The commit says "Hint 1 no longer lists the answer as one of two or three options", but two hints still do. The goalie character item (band1-stories.ts:233) asks "Is he blaming Sofia or helping her?" / "¿Culpa a Sofía o la ayuda?" for the key "He is a leader who supports his team". The seeds+bean-diary pair Q3 (pairs.ts:30) asks "Is it about one seed or about seeds in general?" for the key "The diary tells one girl's experience; the article explains how seeds sprout in general".
unfixed.fix: Point at the evidence without naming the options: "Read what Jamal says to Sofia. What does it show about him?" and "Who is telling each text, and what is each one about?"

unfixed.finding: minor: Spanish "la Luna está creciente / menguante" is unidiomatic
unfixed.problem: The passage and the pair evidence now say "en fase creciente/menguante", but the distractor in the moon sequence question still says "La Luna está menguante." (band1-info.ts:127). Spanish now differs between the passage and its own choices.
unfixed.fix: "La Luna está en fase menguante."

newProblems: minor: several new hint-2 texts name words without quotation marks, which makes them misread. launch-day point-of-view (band2-poems.ts:58): "Words like tonight and will show something that has not happened yet." reads as "will show" (a verb). water-cycle features (band1-info.ts:310): "at what comes after the word means" / "en lo que sigue a quiere decir" is ungrammatical in Spanish. Also "busca las palabras deja de hacer erupción", "busca las palabras hacen ejercicio", "busca las palabras patas y se hunden". Fix: quote the words (“tonight” and “will”; «quiere decir» or “quiere decir”).

minor (Spanish naturalness): the gender-neutral rewrite of the tamales feelings item (band1-stories.ts:62) uses stilted Spanish: "Con alegría de comérselo, aunque se vea chueco", "Con cansancio de comer tamales", "Con enojo porque la abuela lo guardó". A native speaker would say "Le da gusto comérselo aunque se vea chueco" and "Ya no quiere comer más tamales". Neutral wording that sounds natural is possible.

minor (engine): freshSeeds (learning/engine.ts:235) builds its repeat key from passage, prompt, say, picture and visual only, not the choices or the answer. 14 skills give the same prompt for every seed (in 40 seeds: e.dictionary.order, e.commas, e.capitals, e.semicolon.colon, e.intro.commas, e.nonrestrictive, e.parallel.structure, e.dialogue.punctuation, e.abstract.nouns, e.coordinate.adjectives, e.titles.letters, e.thesis, e.nouns.verbs, m.irrational). For those, every slot after the first counts as a repeat, uses up 100 draws × levels, then falls back to a random seed. That means no repeat protection plus extra cost: building one practice set plus a check took 50 ms for e.dictionary.order on desktop, and more on low-end phones. Fix: add the sorted choice labels and the answer text to the key, or skip the redraw when a skill's first few seeds all give the same key.

minor (accessibility): on a reading item the Runner focuses the question h1 with preventScroll. The h1 comes after the passage in the page, so a screen reader hears only "Problem n of m. <question>", with no cue that a passage is above. Before the fix the whole passage was read, too long but complete. The passage title (h2) and its headings (h3) also come before the page's only h1. Fix: link the passage from the question with aria-describedby or an sr-only "Read the text above, then answer", or focus the passage title first. Consider putting the question heading ahead of the passage headings in the outline.

minor (content validity): two of the ten new e.point.of.view questions test character feelings or change, not point of view (RL.4.6). grandfather-hands "How does the speaker feel about Grandfather?" (band1-poems.ts:60). moon-watch "How does the speaker's view of the missing moon change?" (band1-poems.ts:114), whose key nearly repeats that poem's theme key ("The moon only seems to disappear; it always comes back"). Replace them with speaker or perspective questions, for example what the speaker can and cannot know, or how the speaker's point of view shapes a description.

unfixed.finding: major: all three Spanish courses are labelled 'Inglés' (english-rhymes-syllables-es, english-parts-of-speech-es, english-figurative-es)
unfixed.problem: None of the fix commits touch this. apps/web/src/i18n/es.ts:44 still has "subject.english": "Inglés", and apps/web/src/app/(app)/courses/[courseId]/page.tsx:74 still renders t(`subject.${course.subject}`). So 'Rimas y sílabas', 'Sustantivos, verbos y adjetivos' and 'Lenguaje figurado' still show 'Inglés · <grado>', which tells a parent the course teaches English when it teaches Spanish. Landing and SchoolSection use the same label.
unfixed.fix: Choose the label by the course's language: a subject 'english' course with locale 'es' shows 'Lengua' (or 'Lectura y escritura'), and English-language courses keep 'Inglés'. If this is being left for later on purpose, record that decision before the Spanish courses ship.

unfixed.finding: major (partly fixed): the ready-made matcher still says 'A ready-made course already covers this' for common requests
unfixed.problem: The fix only reworded titles and summaries. The 7 cited probes now pass. But the live path, readyMadeMatch (apps/web/src/lib/source-course.ts:374, called from components/generation/Draft.tsx:215), still offers a course when it shares just one stem word with the request: same subject, within 3 grades. Probing about 240 en/es requests at grades K–6 against bda48c5, these still hit the K–5 courses (subject english): 'capital letters' (K–4) -> Sound it out; 'write a short story' (grade 4) and 'short poems' (K–4) -> Sound it out; 'write my name' and 'writing his name' (K–5) -> Nouns, verbs and adjectives; 'english as a second language' (1–6) -> Figurative language; 'word meaning' and 'meaning of words' (1–2) -> Figurative language, a grade 4 course; 'qué pasa en el cuento' (es, K–5) -> Sustantivos, verbos y adjetivos. Taking 'words' out of these summaries only moved the problem elsewhere: 'sight words', 'spelling words', 'root words' and 'word families' at grades 4–5 now match english-context-clues. 'word families' at K–1 now gets no match, even though Sound it out has a whole Word families lesson.
unfixed.fix: Fix the matcher itself, as the original finding suggested. Require 2 or more shared words, or one word that only a few courses use (tutor-demo's coursesWith(w) <= 3 already does this). Prefer the learner's band. Add the probes above to english-k5.test.ts.

unfixed.finding: minor (partly fixed): the `practice` maps are still not used anywhere
unfixed.problem: The new test checks that every lesson key and skill id exists, and the ids are correct (e.compare.texts is the grade 5 RI.5.9 skill, so the renamed e.paired.texts does not apply here). But nothing in apps/web imports these maps, and the comments now say 'Not linked from the lesson screen yet', so the practice links still do nothing. Lesson authors-purpose still has no link.
unfixed.fix: Connect the maps to the 'practice this' step at the end of a lesson, or remove them. Math and science courses use the same pattern, so this is one decision for the whole catalogue.

newProblems: New matcher false positive caused by the fix. The new Sound it out summary ('Phonics: blend letter sounds into cat, sun and pig. Then try short stories.') adds the stem 'stori'. readyMadeMatch now offers Sound it out, a grade 1 phonics course, for 'stories', 'bedtime stories' and 'write stories' at grades K–4 (en, subject english or other). At d34f845 these returned null at K–2, and 'write stories' at grades 3–4 got english-paragraph. So a grade 3–4 parent asking for story writing is told a grade 1 phonics course already covers it, and one click enrols the child. The course also has no stories, only the three-sentence 'Ben and the bug'. Fix: drop 'Then try short stories.' (or fix the matcher as above) and add these probes to english-k5.test.ts.

Over-correction in english-short-words.ts lesson short-vowels. Slide s1 went from 'The letters a, e, i, o and u are vowels.' to 'Some letters are called vowels. Each word below starts with a vowel.' But project step 2 still says 'Write the five vowels on small slips.', and the lesson never says which five letters they are. Reading letter names aloud is correct when the text is naming letters; the read-aloud problem was only about modelling sounds. The new `lone` regex in english-k5.test.ts now bans every letter name in these courses. Fix: change the step to 'Write the first letter of apple, egg, igloo, octopus and up on small slips.', or bring back the vowel-letter line and exempt letter names from the test.

english-parts-of-speech-es.ts nouns s2 bullet: 'Los nombres como Ana no se cuentan. Igual son sustantivos.' In much of Latin America 'igual' here means 'aun así', but in Spain it means 'quizá'. 'No se cuentan' can also be read as 'they don't count'. So one reading is 'names don't count; maybe they are nouns'. Suggest: 'Ana no se puede contar, pero también es un sustantivo.'

Minor: quiz keys now follow the same order lesson after lesson. Overall positions are balanced (29/36/32/2 of 99 at choices 1/2/3/4; no course has more than 5 at any one position). But english-figurative and english-figurative-es use keys [1,2,0] in idioms and personification-hyperbole and for the first three questions of similes-metaphors. english-parts-of-speech and its Spanish twin use [2,1,0] in both adjectives and sentence-parts. A learner can learn 'second, third, first'. Fix: vary the order in each lesson, or add the optional seeded shuffle in QuizView.
cat-eng-k5.verdict: Mostly fixed, but not closed. Setup note: the session's working folder was the user's main checkout on branch foundation, so I did not run git reset --hard there. I audited in detached worktrees at bda48c5 and d34f845 (node_modules APFS-cloned) and removed both afterwards. The main checkout is untouched, nothing was committed, and my scratch files are deleted. Fixed and checked: (1) The CI blocker: vitest src/catalogue passes 12/12, the full web suite passes 4094/4094, and next typegen + tsc and eslint src/catalogue are clean. (2) Answer-position bias: the first choice is the key 29 of 99 times, and the new test enforces the spread. (3) Spoken letter names: no K–2 English line names a lone letter or word part any more. Sounds are named by keyword ('the first sound in sock', 'the egg sound') and every changed key is right; I hand-checked blends, swaps, syllable counts and rhymes (elefante 4, tiger 2, etc.). (4) The Spanish noun test now asks what the word names and whether you can count it, and q1 uses come/muy as wrong answers. (5) All the minor findings are fixed: hyperbole feelings in EN and ES, 'In words like cat', prompts that printed the answer, hints that gave it away, Clasifica, Está distraído, crujía, ser un juego de niños, article-free adjective sentences, a dots step before the rhyme sorts, and the sea otter wording (NOAA says more than a million hairs per square inch; Guinness says densest fur of any mammal, 650,000 to 1.03 million). Still open: the 'Inglés' label on the Spanish courses (major, untouched); the matcher fix, which only reworded summaries, so other single-word false matches remain and the new 'short stories' summary adds one ('write stories' at grades 3–4 now gets the grade 1 phonics course); and the practice maps, which are still not used. Small new wording problems: the short-vowels project asks for 'the five vowels', which the lesson no longer names, and the Spanish bullet 'Igual son sustantivos' reads differently in Spain and Latin America.

unfixed.finding: Theme-statement template (major): items can be solved without reading the passage
unfixed.problem: Fixed at level 1 but not at level 2. I re-ran the original audit's no-read rule over 600 seeds: drop topics of 3 words or fewer, drop choices that name characters, drop absolute claims, prefer 'can'/'deserve'. It scores 42-49% at L1 (was 87%) and still 74-82% at L2 (was 80-95%). 7 of the 8 L2 keys still hedge: 'can' in interpreter, radio-hands, ninety-first, perfect-picture, snow-day and two-tongues, and 'deserve' in night-shift. Only rumor-snowball's key is firm. The contradicts-text wrong choices still carry absolutes: radio-hands 'can never be repaired', rumor-snowball 'always found out', ninety-first 'always leads' and 'only counts', two-tongues 'never fully belong', night-shift 'should ever notice'. 6 of the 8 L2 items fall to the rule. The new guard only counts the topic+plot tags and the swaps-texts tag, so it cannot see this.
unfixed.fix: In l2-stories.ts and l2-poems-primary.ts, state 3-4 of the L2 keys firmly (no can/deserve). Put hedges into more wrong choices, and remove never/always/only from the contradicts-text choices in radio-hands, ninety-first, two-tongues and night-shift. Add a test that runs this no-read rule over the theme.statement bank per level and locale and fails above about 40%.

unfixed.finding: Hint 3 reads out the sentence the key restates (major)
unfixed.problem: Two of the listed items still do this in English. (1) monarch-relay compare.agree, L1 en. Hint 3 quotes “to a mountain forest you have never seen” and “none of the travelers has ever been there before”; the key is 'The monarchs flying south have never been to the forests before.' (2) clock-debate compare.agree, L2 en. Hint 3 quotes “Nearly everyone agrees the switching should stop” and “Stop switching, yes.”; the key is 'The country should stop changing the clocks twice a year.' The Spanish versions now rule out instead. The new repeats() check counts only exact words of 5+ letters at 40%, so it misses synonyms (switching/changing), plurals (forests/forest) and short words. Other items in the same class that still read the evidence: low-tide theme.develop en ('the sigh … wanted to take back' vs key '…take back his sigh'), second-chair theme.develop en/es ('cross the hallway'), mill-letter infer.what en/es ('grown used to it' / 'me he acostumbrado'), library-saturdays pov.response es (the English rules out), comets-asteroids infer.what es (the English rules out). The test's share() has the same blind spots, so it passes all of these.
unfixed.fix: In reading-69.ts, compare stems (for example the first 5 letters of words of 3+ letters, stopwords removed) instead of exact 5+ letter words, or let a question supply its own hint 3. Use the same stemmed measure in reading-69.test.ts, and add the two English items above as named regression cases.

unfixed.finding: Apollo 13 / polio both had two defensible structures (major) - polio residue
unfixed.problem: Apollo 13 is fixed. Polio is mostly fixed: the title is now 'Polio in America, 1952 to 1979' and every paragraph opens with a date. But the passage still runs problem (paragraph 1) to solution (the vaccines ended its spread), and its own explanation says 'The vaccine answers a problem.' A learner who picks 'Problem and solution' gets the misread-as-problem-solution feedback, 'the passage does not mainly present ways to fix it.' That is false for this passage.
unfixed.fix: Give polio's problem-solution choice its own feedback, for example 'It does solve a problem, but the paragraphs are arranged by date'. Or soften paragraph 1's problem framing further.

unfixed.finding: Tutor check_answer 80-character limit (minor, outside the strand)
unfixed.problem: Unchanged. apps/web/src/lib/ai/tools.ts still has answer: z.string().max(80) and an exact label match. 159 of the 430 reading keys (both locales) are still over 80 characters, so a key read aloud fails validation, and a letter or a paraphrase gets index -1.
unfixed.fix: As originally proposed: accept a choice letter or number, or a normalized prefix match, with a higher limit for choice items. Note in answer.ts that choice items are checked by index.

unfixed.finding: Single RL/RI standard codes for mixed literary/informational skills (minor)
unfixed.problem: Only a code comment was added. The codes are unchanged (e.e.paired.texts RI.8.9, e.word.choice RL.6.4, e.inference.evidence RL.6.1, e.central.summary RI.6.2), and the test pins them. This is blocked on a teacher's decision, not done.
unfixed.fix: A teacher chooses the codes, or the skill lists both the RL and RI codes, for example RL.8.9/RI.8.9 for the paired texts.

newProblems: Comparison items have a new length giveaway that beats the one it replaced. Look at the 22 compare.differ/compare.approach item-locales where two choices are clear look-alikes: the swap mirror, or the new near-miss that copies the key's first clause. The key is in that pair every time, and it is the longer of the two in 18 of 22. The two exceptions are museum-return differ and approach. Mirrors were shortened by dropping words ('Text 2, moving.', 'Which time to keep: … Text 2, standard time.', 'the poem, numbers and research'), so the clipped choice is the wrong one. 'Pick the longer of the two look-alikes' now scores about 82% on these items; before the fix it was 50% (keys tied their mirrors). Affected: phone-pouches differ/approach, monarch-relay approach, science-fair approach, lantern-reviews differ, clock-debate differ, wall-opens differ/approach, city-coyotes differ. The near-miss replacements (phone-pouches approach, wall-opens differ, museum-return differ, clock-debate approach) also keep the 'key is one of the two alike choices' 50/50. The new length-rank test looks only at absolute rank, so it misses this. Fix: make the key the shorter one in about half the pairs, write mirrors as full parallel sentences, and add a test on key length versus the most similar choice.

unfixed.problem: The cue was overcorrected, not removed. The key is now strictly the longest in 23/358 entries in English (6%) and 26/358 in Spanish (7%), where chance is about 95/358 (26%). In most entries one distractor was padded to be just longer than the key: the median gap is 6 characters, for example climate #8 key 76 vs 78 characters, earth.energy #2 key 58 vs 60. The key is now the second-longest choice in 201/358 entries in English (56%) and 197/358 in Spanish (55%), against about 26% by chance. It is among the two longest in 75% of entries, against 53% by chance. A learner who always picks the second-longest choice scores 12/13 on s.earth.energy, 12/13 on s.claim.evidence (11/13 in Spanish), 11/13 on s.climate.impact, 13/16 on s.design.criteria, 10/13 on s.carrying.capacity, and 10/14 each on natural.selection, geologic.time and fossil.evidence. The new test at apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more.test.ts:194 only bounds 'strictly longest ≤35%' and 'strictly shortest ≤40%', so it passes this pattern.

Vary which choice is longest. Add a test that, for every bank level and both languages, no length rank (1st, 2nd, …) holds the key in more than about 40% of entries, and that a 'pick the k-th longest' strategy scores at most chance + 10 points.

Most glossary strategies were rewritten as methods. Several still contain the one word that only the key has (not in the stem, not in any distractor):
- s.natural.selection (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/g8-life.ts:11): 'Ask three things: did the trait vary, could it be inherited, and did some individuals leave more offspring' lists exactly the three distractors of #11 ('Which of these is NOT needed…'), so the key falls out by elimination. The new 'hints 1 and 2 never give away' test needs 75% of the key's content words, so it misses these.

unfixed.finding: minor: wave realism, ripple tank (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/physics.ts:170). Partly fixed.
unfixed.problem: Wavelengths are now 2–5 cm and the Spanish says 'cubeta de ondas'. But frequency (5–15 Hz) and wavelength are still drawn independently, so v = f × λ runs from 0.1 to 0.75 m/s. Over 6,000 seeds × en/es, 1,080 of 2,294 ripple items (47%) fall outside 0.2–0.4 m/s: 17% are above 0.5 m/s and 8% are at or below 0.15 m/s. Real ripple-tank water waves travel at about 0.2–0.35 m/s, and a 15 Hz ripple is about 1.5–2 cm long, not 5 cm. The ocean pairs got a dispersion check, but the ripple tank did not.
unfixed.fix: Use fixed (f, λ) pairs that keep v near 0.2–0.35 m/s, for example [5 Hz, 5 cm], [8 Hz, 3.5 cm], [10 Hz, 2.5 cm], [12 Hz, 2 cm]. Or reject draws with f × λ outside [0.2, 0.35], and add a test like the ocean one.

newProblems: major: s.design.criteria (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/g6-earth.ts:468-565) can be solved by picking the odd one out. All 9 criterion/constraint items (#0–#8; #0–#6 rewritten by this fix) have one key and two distractors of the other category. A learner who picks the statement unlike the other two scores 100% without knowing which word is which, so the fix swapped a 50% blind guess for a 100% no-knowledge strategy. In all 7 rewritten items the key's verb form is also the odd one out, in both languages. For example, #0 'It removes…' vs 'can cost…' and 'may use…'; #1 'may be built' vs 'must hold' and 'must stay'; #5 'must be made' vs 'keeps' and 'has'. Fix: give each item 4 choices (1 criterion, 1 constraint and 2 statements that are neither, such as a test result or an opinion), or sometimes ask about the pair ('Which two are constraints?'). Phrase every choice in the same form ('It must …').

minor/moderate: s.body.systems L1 rewritten hint 2 (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/g6-life.ts:328) ends 'the answer is the system they belong to'. That is false for 6 of 14 entries whose answer is an organ, structure or function: #3 small intestine, #7 kidneys, #8 bones' jobs, #10 muscles contract, #12 heart, #13 alveoli. For 'Which organ absorbs most of the nutrients?' it tells the learner to answer with a system. At a warm front the arriving warm air does not lift the cold air; it slides up over it, as entry #7's own clue says. The rewrite also dropped the old strategy's correct fact, 'the warmer air always rises over the colder air'. Fix: 'At a front the warmer air always rises. Ask which air is moving in and how fast the warm air is forced up.'

minor: s.balance.equations L1 hint 3 for single-atom formulas (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/chem.ts:269, `each = f === el ? ""`). This happens in 796 of 6,000 L1 items per language (13%; Na, Mg, Cu, Fe, Al, Hg, Ca, Zn). The fix's own new energy test treats 'hint 3's last number = key' as giving the answer away. Fix: show the step rather than the total, for example 'The right side has 2 Al₂O₃, and each Al₂O₃ has 2 Al atoms.'

minor (Spanish): s.natural.selection giraffe key (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/g8-life.ts:93) was shortened to 'Las jirafas de cuello más largo alcanzaban más alimento y tenían más crías.' It dropped 'que nacían con', while the English key keeps 'born with'. That phrase is what separates the inherited trait from the 'stretched its neck' distractor. minor (Spanish): s.claim.evidence ball-bounce distractor (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/g9-systems.ts:532), 'La pelota rebota cada vez más alto que la altura desde la que la dejan caer.' 'Cada vez más alto' reads as 'higher and higher', which the data (60, 120, 180 cm) actually show, so half the distractor reads as true. minor (science precision): s.resources aquifer key (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/g7-banks.ts:607) was shortened to 'An underground layer of rock or sediment that holds water' to remove the length cue. It dropped 'and lets it flow', which is part of the definition: a layer that holds water but does not pass it on, such as clay, is not an aquifer. Fix: restore 'that holds water and lets it flow' and shorten the distractors instead.

minor, pre-existing (not introduced by this fix, but in a generator the fix edited, and its new Spanish agreement test misses it): the half-life hint 'N ÷ N = 1, así que son 1 vida media.' (apps/web/src/practice/science/upper-more/chem.ts:84 and :141) appears in about 17% of Spanish s.half.life items. Fix: use 'es' when n === 1 ('así que es 1 vida media'), and add the pattern /son 1 / to ES_AGREEMENT.
